outcome: Presence of MNV and Helicobacter in donor dams, weanlings, and adult post-immersion animals
cohort: Newborn litters of various mouse strains, born to dams positive for murine norovirus (MNV) and Helicobacter spp., who were immersed in iodine and then cross-fostered to pathogen-negative Swiss Webster dams.
finding: The iodine immersion combined with cross-fostering technique successfully eradicated murine norovirus (MNV) and Helicobacter spp. in laboratory mice colonies.
followup_time: 18 months (for environmental monitoring of colony status); 8 weeks postweaning (for individual animals)
